openings.claim: A future paper-only assembly table could report which envelope still owes an item before anyone opens it: each envelope owns a counted material reserve, and a leftover item is an omission witness. This could help participants receive their assigned complete kits and reduce the two volunteers' checking burden; the 60-kit outcome remains unproven.
openings.delta: Convert the sample's pattern quantities into per-envelope reserves, with pattern identity pencilled on envelope and tally sheet. Existing tray tags guide reserve preparation. Unlike the incumbent's material labels and rarely consulted samples, an envelope cannot be treated as complete while its reserve has leftovers. This detects filling omissions only, not incorrectly prepared reserves or undetected transfers between envelopes.
openings.prediction: With correctly prepared reserves and exclusive envelope ownership, intentionally withheld filling items leave witnesses identifying the affected envelopes before reopening; omission-free envelopes leave none.
openings.rival_prediction: Local reach reduction alone explains O4. Loose materials beside each volunteer may improve speed, but ordinary unallocated piles cannot identify the particular envelope affected by a withheld item.
openings.defeat: A withheld item produces no correctly attributable leftover, a complete envelope produces a false witness, or reserve preparation creates quantity errors. These defeat the enabling mechanism; excessive setup time or table footprint defeats its workshop feasibility.
openings.probe: Use exactly two volunteers and existing supplies for a reversible twelve-envelope rehearsal capped at twenty minutes, including preparation and checking. Include all three patterns with specified dimensions and quantities, fit everything within the existing table, and compare allocated reserves with equally local unallocated piles. Deliberately withhold recorded items during filling, then identify affected envelopes from leftovers before checking contents. Restore every kit afterward; do not infer 60-kit success from this probe.
assumptions: Per-envelope reserves and opened packets fit the existing table; their footprint is unknown.
Volunteers can prepare accurate reserves without consuming the full 90-minute allowance.
Exclusive reserve ownership can be maintained; aggregate material counts cannot detect compensating cross-envelope transfers.
The small-batch pattern mixture and omission stage remain unknown.
